findings.rationale: AZ's uploaded updates are about 10-20x the median update norm in every round from round 1 onward (size-adjusted median norm ratio 14.0, z=+11.5), and their direction against the median is essentially random: mean cosine 0.06, with per-round cosines swinging between about -0.63 and +0.45. This is the signature of large random noise added to uploads, not a consistent sign-flip or scaling attack. Local performance is normal (AUC 0.837, CITL 0.002), consistent with the 'accuracy barely moves' pattern of explanation_instability. Drift and subgroup screens show nothing for AZ.

WA (the largest client, n_train 11181) uploads updates roughly 14-20x the median norm in every round from round 1 (median norm ratio 18.8, z=+9.2), with near-zero, erratic cosine to the median (mean 0.18, min -0.46). The pattern is persistent random-noise-like uploads rather than a consistent adversarial direction. Its local AUC (0.801) and CITL (0.007) look normal, so the global model's accuracy is not visibly damaged.

WI's updates have a median norm about 12x the median client (z=+10.8 on the size-adjusted norm ratio), and their cosine to the median is near zero on average (mean 0.076, min -0.33, z=-5.3). This matches the same random-noise upload signature as AZ and WA. Local performance is normal (AUC 0.798, CITL 0.003). I had no budget left for a per-round confirmation of WI, so this rests on the all-client screen alone and carries lower confidence.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary, and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then ran per-round checks on the suspects. Three clients (AZ, WA, WI) show a consistent upload anomaly from round 1: update norms 12-19x the median, with cosine to the median near zero and erratic. Their local performance and calibration look normal. I classed this as explanation_instability (random noise in uploads) rather than poisoning, because the cosines are not consistently negative. WI is the least certain, since I could not confirm it per round. Other weak leads were not reported: small clients GU and VI show drift or CITL deviations that are within noise on per-round checks, DC has one drift z of 3.9, and subgroup outliers in GA, CT, WY, CA, NH and TX are small-n noise with no consistent pattern. Budget is fully spent (20.0 used).
